newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks touch historic highs, seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks touch historic highs, seen rising.

text.p: Croatian stocks led by blue chips thrust upward on Tuesday, touching historic highs and were seen as rising further thanks to a mixture of positive impulses on the market.

"The market is bullish," said one trader, adding that the prices of Zagrebacka Banka and drugs firm Pliva were tracing the rise of their global depositary receipts (GDRs) to all-time records in London.
Expectations that confectioner Kras and food processor Podravka might come out with their own GDR issues and list them abroad were pushing their prices up, she said.
Traders predicted that seaside hotelier stocks would also climb amid rumours that foreign investors were buying them.
* Six of eight traded issues rose and two were unchanged.
* The biggest net gainer Kras jumped 44 kuna to close at 399, down one from the 400-kuna all-time peak, on volume of 280 shares. They were issued with a face value of 100 German marks.
* Most active Zagrebacka Banka, with 3,933 units sold, added 40 kuna to 790 after reaching a record high of 800 kuna.
Its GDRs, issued at 10 to each share, were up to $16.25 today from Monday's $15.3 on Seaq International in London.
* Podravka, trading 2,438 shares, rebounded five kuna to 230 after a slight dip last week with reports of a 1995 loss.
* Hotel stocks moved up to all-time highs:
- Jadranturist eight kuna to 185 on volume of 438 shares
- Suncani Hvar five kuna to 40 on volume of 904
- Laguna also added five kuna to 825 with 291 shares sold.
* Pliva flat at 12,200 kuna on volume of 124. Its GDRs, representing 1/50 of each share fetched $48.5 on the London Stock Exchange.
* Electric cables manufacturer Elka also unchanged at 135 with 104 units sold.
* The second tranche of public debt refinancing bonds traded for the first time at 1.07 percent above par for 3.35 million kuna turnover. The bonds pay an annual interest of eight percent.
* Share volume up at 8,512 units. Total turnover also higher at 8.51 million kuna.
* Central bank's exchange rates: 5.3726 kuna = $1, 3.5559 kuna = 1 DM.
